newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco cuts rates on T-bond issues 0.5 pt-Fin Min.
newsitem.headline: Morocco cuts rates on T-bond issues 0.5 pt-Fin Min.

text.p: Morocco has cut by half a point to 9.0 percent the annual interest rate on public Treasury bond issues, Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj said on Thursday.
"We already took the decision to cut by half a point the annual interest rates on public Treasury bonds (emprunts nationaux) to 9.0 percent," Kabbaj told Reuters.
The public Treasury bonds are listed on the Casablanca stock exchange as part of the state domestic debt oriented to the small investors.
The move was apparently aimed at encouraging competition on the market.
"To break with past experience, the public treasury bonds will be opened to all operators in order to stimulate the bond market," Kabbaj said.
In the past, institutional investors were barred from access to the public treasury bond issues, including insurance companies, traders said.
A total of 3.9 billion dirhams as public Treasury bonds were issued by the government in 1995, a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
The new government decision aligns the public treasury bonds interest rate with the Bank al-Maghrib (central bank) rate, he added.
The bank issues a 52-week Treasury bill at 9.0 percent interest rate, every Wednesday.
Total domestic borrowing more than doubled in 1995 to 13 billion dirhams from 5.2 billion dirhams in 1994, a recent report issued by Bank al-Maghrib said.
